subject: Vulnerability management evidence request for SIG/SOC2 — scan cadence & CVE SLA
messages:
From: Andrea Lopez <andrealopez@finserve.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finserve.com
Date: 2028-04-10T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Vulnerability management evidence for SIG/SOC2 review

Hi Redwood team,

We're preparing for a SIG and SOC 2 update and need a compact package of vulnerability management evidence for the control review. Can you confirm you can provide the following by end of next week (EOD Apr 17)?

Requested items (concise):
- Signed VM attestation (DocuSign) that lists scan cadence and SLA commitments.
- Sample weekly authenticated scan export (JSON or CSV).
- A short statement describing scan cadence (authenticated, unauthenticated, dynamic) and which assets are in each cadence.
- CVE remediation SLA table (Critical/High/Medium) and an example closure ticket.
- Evidence links: one sample scan export, the corresponding ticket/PR, and a high-level remediation playbook excerpt.

If anything above is a problem or requires legal sign-off, flag it and let us know the expected turn time. We can also take a short (30 min) walkthrough if that helps.

Thanks — we aim to include this in our SIG baseline.

Andrea Lopez
Security Manager, FinServe
andrea.lopez@finserve.com
security@finserve.com

Thanks Andrea — received and noted.

Monica / Laura, I'm taking point to assemble the bundle for FinServe. Plan and immediate asks below:

Plan (deliver by 2028-04-13 EOD):
- Monica: produce the sample scan export (weekly authenticated) and vm-scan-index.csv with asset coverage mapping; include a sample ticket/PR for a recently closed Critical.
- Monica: draft remediation SLA statement outlining our CVE timelines (we'll include examples).
- Laura: quick review of attestation language and sign-off for DocuSign.
- I'll assemble the Drive folder, run a fast QA of artifacts, and send DocuSign link to Andrea.

Proposed artifacts we'll attach:
- monthly-scan-sample-20280331.json (sample weekly export + metadata)
- vm-scan-index.csv (asset -> scanner -> cadence)
- remediation-sla-statement.pdf (official SLA language; draft attached)
- VM-Attestation-for-FinServe-draft.pdf (DocuSign-ready once legal OKs)

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1GzR-example-finserve-evidence (I will populate). HubSpot deal: HS-55678 (for reference).

If there are objections to the proposed SLA bullets below, call them out — otherwise we'll include them in the attestation draft:
- Critical (CVSS >= 9.0): initial mitigation or compensating control within 24 hours; documented mitigation plan within 72 hours; full remediation (patch or approved compensating control) within 10 business days for infra-owned systems and within 30 calendar days for third-party library upgrades.
- High (7.0-8.9): mitigation within 72 hours; remediation within 30 calendar days.
- Medium/Low: tracked with standard patch windows (30-90 days depending on severity).

Monica — can you attach a sample Jira ticket and the scan export to the Drive folder when ready? Laura — can you review the attestation text by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
Aditya
Director, Solutions (Redwood Inference)

Attachment: remediation-sla-statement.pdf (draft)

On Tue, Apr 10, 2028 at 11:02 AM Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com> wrote:
> Monica — can you attach a sample Jira ticket and the scan export to the Drive folder when ready?

Aditya / Laura — copying in the technical details we plan to include in the attestation and evidence bundle. I'll upload the artifacts to the Drive folder by EOD 2028-04-11.

Scan cadence (summary to include in attestation):
- Authenticated agent-based scans: weekly for managed infra (hosts with Redwood-managed agents).
- Unauthenticated network scans: nightly passive collection + a rolling nightly Quick Scan pass across public interfaces.
- Dynamic/prioritized scans (DAST/interactive): scheduled monthly for customer-facing services and after major releases.
- Third-party dependency scans (SCA): continuous on PRs; full repo sweep weekly.

Asset coverage note: the vm-scan-index.csv maps asset tags (service, env, region) to scanner type and cadence. We'll include a short README in the Drive folder.

CVE remediation SLA (precise wording for the attestation):
- Critical (CVSS >= 9.0 OR exploited in the wild):
  - Initial mitigation or compensating control implemented within 24 hours of detection/notification.
  - Documented remediation plan posted to ticket within 72 hours.
  - Target for full remediation (patch/upgrade or validated compensating control): 10 business days for infrastructure/managed services; 30 calendar days for third-party library upgrades where safe upgrade paths require coordination.
- High (7.0 - 8.9):
  - Compensating mitigation within 72 hours.
  - Full remediation target within 30 calendar days.
- Medium/Low: staged into the regular patch cycle (30-90 days depending on category).

Evidence we'll upload (attached in Drive and included in the DocuSign packet):
- monthly-scan-sample-20280331.json (sample export from our authenticated scanner with metadata).
- vm-scan-index.csv (mapping and coverage).
- Example Jira ticket: SUP-4092 (Critical CVE closure: includes PR/patch link).
- remediation-sla-statement.pdf (finalized wording).
- VM-Attestation-for-FinServe-draft.pdf (DocuSign-ready; Laura — please review).

Notes on verification: we will include the scanned export + the ticket history and the PR/merge commit that closed the vulnerability. For third-party libraries, we will include a link to the dependency PR and the release notes demonstrating the fix.

I'll attach the files now.

Monica Patel
Security Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
